title: Gaia DR3 and ZTF timing of 11,668 Mira-like stars (2014-2025) shows a weak persistent period-change signal and no confirmed rapid period change; a simple O-C extrapolation test is biased
abstract: Question: do the pulsation periods of faint Gaia DR3 long-period variables change between Gaia DR3 (2014.6-2017.4) and ZTF DR24 (2018.2-2025.8), and does any star show a rapid change (|dP/dt|/P >= 1%/yr) like the thermal-pulse Mira T UMi? Method: we made ZTF r O-C curves of 11,668 large-amplitude LPVs (Dec > -28, G 12.5-18.5) and timed their Gaia G epochs with each star's ZTF template. We applied two population tests. Test A compares the Gaia phase offset with the extrapolated ZTF O-C curvature. Test B compares the within-ZTF period change with the Gaia-to-ZTF change and has no shared Gaia/ZTF term. We compared both tests with light-curve-level simulations (real sampling; cycle-length, amplitude and mean-level jitter) and with injections. Results: Test A gave rho = 0.28 in a 360-star pilot. A Gaussian O-C null gave 0.00 +- 0.06, but noise-only light-curve simulations give correlations of the same size and sign pattern as the full data (data 0.195 vs null 0.122 in well-sampled stars). Thus Test A is dominated by a sampling artifact. In Test B, well-sampled stars give rho = 0.080 [0.049, 0.109] (0.095 with DR3 catalogue periods), against -0.047 for noise only and 0.81 for a constant dP/dt population. Thus a small part of the measured period change persists over about 10 years. The spread of the within-ZTF period change is not larger than in the noise-only simulation. The conservative 95% bound is sd(dP/dt/P) <= 0.39%/yr. Four stars pass a strict rapid-change rule, against 0 of 2,594 simulated noise-only stars. But all four are faint, very red, poorly sampled plane or bulge Miras, two have close Gaia neighbours, and their Gaia phases and earlier OGLE/VSX periods do not follow a monotonic change. We list them as a watch list, not as thermal-pulse candidates. Limitations: simulation jitter settings are approximate, blending and censoring of faint minima are not simulated, and bright Miras are outside the sample.

display.caption: Spearman rho (95% bootstrap CI) for Test A (Gaia phase offset vs ZTF O-C extrapolation) and Test B (Gaia-to-ZTF period change vs within-ZTF change). Blue and orange: data. Grey: light-curve simulation with no period change. Green: simulation with constant dP/dt/P ~ N(0, 1%/yr). Test A follows the noise-only simulation. Test B is positive only in well-sampled stars and is about 10 times smaller than for a constant-dP/dt population.

Distribution of the within-ZTF fractional period change (P second half - P first half)/P for data (blue), the noise-only simulation (grey) and the 1%/yr constant-dP/dt simulation (green), by sampling class. The data are not wider than the noise-only simulation.

ZTF r O-C (points, relative to the linear ZTF ephemeris), the quadratic fit extrapolated back, and the Gaia DR3 G timing offset (orange square) for the four stars that pass the rapid-change rule. The Gaia offsets do not follow the extrapolation, so the stars are not confirmed.
